description: Guidance for Thin-Layer Sediment Placement is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by National Estuarine Research Reserve System | Science Collaborative; NOAA, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; University of Michigan | Graham Sustainability Institute | Water Center. Tidal marshes provide key ecosystem services, but they are threatened by sea level rise. For some of these ecosystems to survive, it will require active management to increase tidal marsh resilience. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Flooding – Coastal, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems. Assets: Natural Areas and Wildlife. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
